description: Keep the sticky Info / Cargo section navigator synchronized with the section a player is manually reading, so its active destination remains useful while scrolling the long mobile guide.
steps: Use and consult miner-daily-task-runner before implementing; run ./init.sh before development, preserve the React-before-runtime startup order, and retain existing DOM IDs/classes consumed by src/dom.ts and src/game.ts.

Inspect src/ui.tsx, src/game.ts Info / Cargo open-close and navigation handlers, src/info-navigation.ts, src/styles.css, and existing UI/startup tests. Extract a DOM-free helper for resolving the active section from section positions/visibility rather than embedding ordering decisions in DOM mutation code.

Wire the Info / Cargo dialog so scrolling its card updates exactly one existing [data-info-section] button with aria-current, while button-driven focus/scroll navigation, opening on Objective & Cargo, Escape/backdrop/close behavior, and focus restoration to the game remain intact. Avoid changing the stable section IDs or blocking normal card scrolling.

Add focused unit coverage for the active-section helper and a DOM/runtime regression for active-nav updates after a manual card scroll. Ensure observer/listener lifecycle is safe across repeated modal open/close calls and does not update a hidden dialog.

Use ./init.sh and run desktop plus 390×844 headless CDP smokes that start the game, open Info / Cargo, manually scroll through Objective, Stats, Prospecting, Hazards, and Controls, verify the matching active navigator label each time, close the modal, resume keyboard movement, and collect runtime exceptions.
acceptance: While manually scrolling the long Info / Cargo guide, players always have one visible active navigator button that accurately names the section currently being read; activating a navigator button still scrolls and focuses its target.
The dialog remains scrollable and accessible on desktop and a 390×844 phone viewport; close/Escape/backdrop behavior, modal layering, focus restoration, and movement controls do not regress.
DOM-free helper and UI/runtime regression coverage pass, and browser smokes report no runtime exceptions.
Before marking complete, follow miner-daily-task-runner and run ./init.sh, ./test.sh, npm test, npm run typecheck, and npm run build as fresh final verification.

description: Declutter the gameplay HUD by removing nonessential persistent hint text so the mine and player remain visible, especially on phone screens.
steps: Use and consult miner-daily-task-runner before implementing; run ./init.sh before development, preserve the React-before-runtime startup order, and retain required DOM IDs/classes consumed by src/dom.ts and src/game.ts unless the corresponding runtime path is deliberately removed or relocated.

Audit the always-visible HUD copy in src/ui.tsx, src/dom.ts, src/game.ts, and src/styles.css, including objective, terrain scanner, fuel reserve, depth milestone, cargo feedback, service status, and sound-status text. Identify which messages are redundant tutorial/hint text rather than essential real-time instruments, actions, or safety warnings.

Remove the nonessential always-visible hint widgets from gameplay rather than merely shrinking them. Keep core meters, cash/depth, actionable depot controls, temporary toast feedback, and urgent low-fuel/game-state warnings usable; move any retained optional explanation into the on-demand Info / Cargo screen where appropriate.

Reflow desktop and 390×844 phone HUD layouts so no remaining panel obscures a large portion of the canvas or covers the player’s normal play area. Preserve touch/keyboard controls, button reachability, status updates, and modal layering.

Update DOM/runtime and React-shell tests for the intentional reduced HUD surface, then use ./init.sh for desktop and phone headless CDP visual/layout smokes that start play, move and mine, exercise depot controls, trigger a low-fuel warning if practical, open/close Info / Cargo, and collect runtime exceptions.
acceptance: During normal play, redundant persistent hint text no longer covers the mine; the gameplay canvas is substantially clearer on desktop and a 390×844 phone viewport.
Essential live information and actions remain available: cash/depth, fuel/hull/cargo meters, depot/shop controls, temporary action feedback, and urgent low-fuel or game-state warnings.
Any retained explanatory guidance is optional/on-demand instead of occupying the gameplay view, and keyboard/touch controls plus Info / Cargo behavior do not regress.

Updated tests pass and desktop/mobile browser smokes show a clear playable HUD with no runtime exceptions. Before marking complete, follow miner-daily-task-runner and run ./init.sh, ./test.sh, npm test, npm run typecheck, and npm run build as fresh final verification.

description: Profile and remove the underground gameplay lag so deep mining stays responsive without reducing core gameplay feedback.
steps: Use and consult miner-daily-task-runner before implementing; run ./init.sh before development and preserve React-before-runtime startup ordering plus existing gameplay controls and save behavior.

Reproduce the issue in a served browser at a meaningful underground depth on desktop and a 390×844 phone viewport. Capture frame-time/FPS evidence and isolate the dominant hot paths before changing behavior, including the requestAnimationFrame loop, HUD DOM updates, particle work, active-enemy work, and canvas terrain rendering.

Inspect src/game.ts and src/renderer.ts, where every frame currently redraws a visible tile window with per-tile gradients, procedural blobs/strata, canvas save/restore calls, and repeated HUD formatting/DOM writes. Implement the smallest measured optimization(s), such as caching or simplifying static underground terrain art, culling/bounding particles or offscreen work, and throttling unchanged HUD writes, while retaining visual readability and game rules.

Add focused deterministic tests for extracted performance policy/helpers where practical and keep rendering changes isolated from world generation, collision, ore, hazard, enemy, fuel, and extraction logic.

Use ./init.sh for fresh desktop and 390×844 headless CDP performance smokes that start a game, descend/mine into underground terrain, keep moving/drilling through an extended sample, report frame timing/FPS or long-frame counts, exercise Info / Cargo open-close, and collect runtime exceptions.
acceptance: Underground mining and movement are visibly smoother than the measured baseline on desktop and a 390×844 phone viewport, with no sustained severe frame stalls during normal play.
Optimizations are based on captured profiling evidence rather than a speculative broad rewrite, and their trade-offs are documented in progress.txt.
Terrain readability, particles/feedback within reasonable bounds, controls, HUD essentials, mining/economy, enemies, saves, and Info / Cargo behavior remain functional.

Updated tests pass and performance smokes report no runtime exceptions. Before marking complete, follow miner-daily-task-runner and run ./init.sh, ./test.sh, npm test, npm run typecheck, and npm run build as fresh final verification.

description: Replace the Info / Cargo modal's scroll-navigation buttons with actual accessible tabs so players switch directly between one focused panel at a time.
steps: Use and consult miner-daily-task-runner before implementing; run ./init.sh before development, preserve React-before-runtime startup ordering, and retain existing content/runtime hooks such as cargo, objective, stats, prospecting, hazards, and controls.

Replace the current navigation-to-scroll behavior in src/ui.tsx, src/game.ts, and src/info-navigation.ts with a WAI-ARIA tab pattern: a tablist containing role=tab buttons with stable IDs, aria-selected, aria-controls, roving tabindex, and matching role=tabpanel content. Selecting a tab must show only its panel rather than merely scrolling a long card.

Implement pointer, keyboard arrow-key, Home/End, Enter/Space, focus, open/close, Escape, backdrop, and focus-restoration behavior. Default to the Objective & Cargo tab when opening; ensure runtime updates still refresh cargo/objective/stats whether or not their panel is active.

Remove or adapt the old sticky scroll navigator and active-section resolver only where they are no longer applicable, keeping the modal compact and usable on desktop and a 390×844 phone viewport. Do not reintroduce HUD obstruction or make active panel content inaccessible.

Add DOM-free tab-selection helper coverage plus React shell/runtime regressions for ARIA relationships, panel visibility, keyboard navigation, and modal lifecycle. Use ./init.sh for desktop and phone CDP smokes that switch every tab, observe the correct panel/cargo update, close the modal, resume movement, and collect runtime exceptions.
acceptance: Info / Cargo presents clear, actual tabs; activating one displays only its corresponding content panel rather than scrolling through a combined guide.

Tabs conform to the expected accessible semantics and keyboard behavior: tablist/tab/tabpanel roles, aria-selected, aria-controls, roving focus, arrow navigation, Home/End, and Enter/Space activation.

All existing Cargo, Stats, Prospecting, Hazards, and Controls content remains reachable and live game values update correctly; close/Escape/backdrop behavior, focus restoration, touch controls, and gameplay do not regress.

Updated tests pass and desktop/390×844 browser smokes report no runtime exceptions. Before marking complete, follow miner-daily-task-runner and run ./init.sh, ./test.sh, npm test, npm run typecheck, and npm run build as fresh final verification.

description: Zoom the gameplay camera out by 25% so players can see more of the mine and nearby hazards while moving underground.
steps: Use and consult miner-daily-task-runner before implementing; run ./init.sh before development and preserve the fixed 960×640 world-to-canvas coordinate model, controls, collision, HUD, and touch targeting.

Audit the effective camera scale across src/constants.ts, src/dom.ts, src/renderer.ts, and touch-coordinate helpers. Confirm the existing tile/camera values against a live baseline rather than relying on comments, then make the final visible mine view 25% more zoomed out than the pre-task baseline.

Adjust the camera/tile scale through shared constants and/or rendering math rather than CSS-only canvas stretching. Preserve correct world bounds, camera following, ship position, particle placement, enemy rendering, surface/depot art, and pointer/touch direction calculations.
Review HUD and modal overlays after the expanded field of view so they do not obscure the additional useful play area, especially on a 390×844 phone viewport.

Add focused math/regression coverage for viewport tile coverage or scale-derived coordinate behavior, then use ./init.sh for desktop and phone CDP smokes that start play, descend/mine, verify substantially more surrounding tiles are visible, exercise touch/keyboard movement and Info / Cargo open-close, and collect runtime exceptions.
acceptance: The live game camera is 25% more zoomed out than the verified pre-task baseline, showing a materially larger surrounding mine area on desktop and a 390×844 phone viewport.
Player movement, drilling, collisions, camera bounds/following, touch direction mapping, surface/depot rendering, particles, enemies, and HUD alignment remain correct at the new scale.
The expanded view improves visibility without introducing canvas blur, clipping, empty-border artifacts, or renewed HUD obstruction.

Updated tests pass and desktop/mobile browser smokes report no runtime exceptions. Before marking complete, follow miner-daily-task-runner and run ./init.sh, ./test.sh, npm test, npm run typecheck, and npm run build as fresh final verification.
